# PR #3505: Patch: card tests build helper units from stand-in ids that spell out their cost and stats, so no comment restates a real card's numbers

Closes #3486

The last "stopped" notice came from a wait loop I no longer needed. The checks it was waiting on (catalog, patches, spec) had already finished and passed. Nothing needs to run again.

## What changed

**Stand-in cards (engine testkit).** A card test that needs only a card's numbers now names a card whose id spells them out:
- Units: `"stand-in (3) 9/9"`, `"stand-in (1) 4/4 R12/12"`, `"stand-in (4) 7/7 Armor 7"`, `"stand-in (1) 3/3 Rush, First Strike"`.
- Cards with no text: `"stand-in (0) Spell"`, `"stand-in (2) Field Spell"`, `"stand-in (1) Trap"`.

How it works:
- **New file:** `crates/engine/src/testkit/stand_in.rs` holds the grammar (`STAND_IN_GRAMMAR`), the parser and a thread-local cache. A malformed id panics, and the message gives the grammar.
- **`catalog::find_def`** keeps its lookup order. The catalog part of it moved unchanged into a new `catalog_def`. On a miss, `find_def` asks `stand_in`:
  - under `testkit`, `stand_in` builds the card from the id and caches it, leaked the same way `register_catalog` leaks;
  - without `testkit` it returns `None`, so production builds compile none of it.
- **The cache stays out of `registered()`.** So no `query`, random pool, `def_by_index` or deck validation can reach a stand-in, and no seeded draw moves.
- **`scenario.rs`** resolves a stand-in id to itself (`def_ids_for`), and `describe_instance` gives its name.
- **Docs:** SURFACE §8, `docs/ADDING_CARDS.md` §2 ("Helper cards"), and the engine README's `testkit` row.

**`cargo jackioh names` covers the card tests** (`crates/tools/src/names.rs`):
- It walks every `.rs` file under `crates/cards/src` and `crates/cards/tests`. In a script's own file it starts at the `#[cfg(test)]` line.
- A helper line is `const <NAME>: &str = "<id>"; // <comment>` with a catalog id. Its comment takes the card's name: `// Hit Job` or `// Hit Job: the removal`.
- A comment beside a catalog id that gives a cost (`(N)`, `(X)`) or stats (`A/H`, `+2/+2`, `R12/12`, `3X/3X`) is an error naming its file and line. Such a comment is refused, not compared with the catalog, so there is nothing to keep in sync.
- A new `jackioh-tools` test, `card_tests_pass_names_check`, runs the check over the whole tree under `cargo test`. The tools README's `names` row is updated.

**The migration** (`crates/cards`, test code only, 573 files). A script compared every changed line with `main`. It found only two kinds of change, all inside test modules or test files:
- 389 helper ids now name stand-ins.
- 2,066 comments were rewritten to give no numbers and to start with the card's name.

Comments beside a stand-in no longer repeat what the id now spells out: the cost, the stats, the keywords and the replaced card's name. Most of those comments were dropped. The ones that also said what the helper does in the test kept that part.

## How it was tested

All run in this worktree:
- **Engine:**
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --lib stand_in`: 9 passed.
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test rules_3 stand_in`: 3 passed. These tests:
    - play, attack and summon stand-ins from hand, field, backrow and library;
    - check that no `query`, `registered_catalog()` or `def_by_index` returns a stand-in;
    - check that a seeded pool draw comes out the same whether the zones hold fixture cards or stand-ins.
- **Cards:**
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-cards --no-fail-fast`: 8,520 + 1,106 passed, 0 failed.
  - The tests of the 12 swaps added in this run were run again after a recompile: 95 passed.
- **Tools:**
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh names::`: 12 passed, including `card_tests_pass_names_check`.
  - `cargo jackioh names --check`: exit 0. `cargo jackioh names`: wrote nothing (`git diff --stat` was the same before and after).
- **Workspace:**
  - `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts`: exit 0, 18,689 passed, 0 failed. `git status --porcelain -- apps/web/src/wire` was empty.
  - The first workspace run failed `acceptance::helpers_each_test_takes_its_shared_helpers_from_their_home`: the new rules test had a local helper named `ids`, the same name as a shared one. I renamed it `pool_ids`, and the acceptance test then passed 35 of 35.
  - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0. After the rename I ran it again for `jackioh-engine` with `testkit`: exit 0.
  - `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- **Repo checks:**
  - `cargo jackioh catalog check`, `patches check`: ok. `spec check`: "1871 rulings, 4834 proofs, 60562 citations in 3942 files, 24833 links: ok".
  - `cargo jackioh golden check`: "hotseat fixture: folds to 512357ea", exit 0.
  - `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200`: exit 0.
  - `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main`: `classify: Internal`. No fragment is added.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

The plan's ten decisions stand:
- the set is Core;
- a Unit with no `R…` part takes R349's Radiant fallback;
- the Radiant face's keywords can be written;
- keywords are written as `keyword_key` writes them;
- a face's text is its keyword line;
- numbers are refused anywhere in the comment;
- a helper with no comment gets none added;
- this is one pull request;
- only helpers with no text become stand-ins;
- tests in other crates are out of scope.

This run added these:
1. **`names` replaces the text before a `: ` only when that text is some catalog card's name.** Otherwise it puts the card's name in front.
   - The plan's rule 3 would have replaced any text before a `: `. That drops the `Cry:`, `Radiant:`, `Aura:` or `Field Spell:` at the start of about 180 existing comments: `// Cry: summon a copy` would have become `// Duplicating Felinors: summon a copy`.
   - What it gives up: a comment that uses a name the card no longer has gets the new name put in front (`Hit Job: Contract Killer: …`), and a person trims it.
2. **Three more helpers with no text became stand-ins:** Genn (`classic-086`), Spikey Steven (`traininggrounds-001`) and Clobberer (`traininggrounds-008`).
   - The plan's list missed them. I kept the plan's exceptions: a file keeps the real card if it names the card's id, its name or `Human`, or reads it from the catalog. Their tests stayed green.
   - Cards whose text is only keywords but that carry more mechanics (AP Rounds, State of the Game, Stratos, the tokens) keep their real ids with a name comment, per decision 9. I did not swap them, because a test can depend on any one of those keywords.
3. **Comments beside stand-ins** lost the cost, stats, keywords and the name of the card the stand-in replaced. A comment was dropped when nothing else was left. `names` does not check them: a stand-in is not a catalog card, and its numbers are its id.
4. **Costs in quoted card text such as "(1) Cost or less" were reworded** ("cheap", "costing 1 or less"), since the check refuses any `(N)`.
   - Numbers that are not the helper's own cost or stats and have no parentheses were kept: "Deal 4 damage", "Flood costs 4 since patch v0.2.0".
   - The helper's own cost in words ("cost 4", "a 4-mana Unit") was dropped too, although the check would not catch it.
5. **`card_test_plan`, used only by the tree test, lives in the tests module of `names.rs`** rather than behind an `#[allow]`.

## Worth a second look

- **The check's core functions** in `crates/tools/src/names.rs`: `card_test_line`, `named_comment` and `gives_numbers`.
- **The panic in `find_def`.** A malformed `stand-in…` id panics there in every `testkit` build, and the tools binary is one of them. No catalog id starts with the prefix (a test pins this), so only a hand-written log that names one can reach it.
- **The 2,066 rewritten comments.** A script drafted them. Seven review agents then corrected them in batches, each batch run through a checker, and I hand-fixed the last dozen. Where a cost threshold had to be reworded, the comment says less than it used to.
- **`cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` was not run.** It needs `--parent-bin`, a release build of `main`, which I did not build on this 4-core runner. Without it, `classify` reports `Internal` and leaves the play-code check undone. CI's `rust (classify)` runs the full check.

   - `"stand-in (0) Spell"`, `"stand-in (2) Field Spell"`, `"stand-in (1) Trap"`: cards with no text, for filler and spares.
